chunks.title: Leverage and liquidation
chunks.text: Leverage means using borrowed funds to take a position larger than one's own capital. With 10x leverage, a 1% price move changes the position's value by about 10% of the trader's margin. If losses reduce the margin below the exchange's maintenance requirement, the position is liquidated: the exchange closes it automatically. Large clusters of liquidations can accelerate price moves, because forced selling or buying adds to the move that triggered them.

chunks.title: Stablecoin
chunks.text: A stablecoin is a cryptocurrency designed to keep a stable value relative to a reference asset, most often the US dollar. Fiat-backed stablecoins such as USDT and USDC hold reserves of cash and short-term instruments. Other designs use crypto collateral or algorithms. Stablecoins are widely used as the quote currency on exchanges, which is why most trading pairs are quoted against USDT. A stablecoin can lose its peg if confidence in its reserves or mechanism breaks down.

chunks.title: News sentiment scoring (VADER)
chunks.text: TickerSage scores recent headlines with VADER, a rule-based sentiment model that combines a word lexicon with rules for punctuation, capitalisation and negation. Each headline gets a compound score from -1 (most negative) to +1 (most positive). Headlines with a compound score of 0.05 or more are labelled positive, -0.05 or less negative, and anything in between neutral. Headline sentiment is a rough summary of tone in recent coverage. It does not prove why a price moved, and correlation between news tone and price moves on a given day is not causation.
